name: Velodash
tagline: App for planning cycling routes and organizing group rides, with route sync to bike computers and live tracking of riders during the ride.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: You can absolutely build yourself a route planner: a map, a drawn line, elevation profile, GPX export, a ride log. That part is a weekend. What you cannot build is the other eight people on Saturday's ride already having the app, accepting the invite, pushing the route to their Garmin, and showing up as dots on a shared map while everyone gets dropped on the climb. Group coordination software is worth exactly as much as the group's adoption of it, and a self-hosted thing you made does not have that. Add head unit sync, which means real integrations with Garmin and Wahoo accounts, and the honest answer is that the personal version solves the easy half.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you draw or import routes on a map, see distance and elevation, save them, and export GPX plus a shareable read-only ride page with a start time and meeting point.
requirements: A map tile source (OpenStreetMap tiles, or a Mapbox/Thunderforest key in .env)
An elevation API key or a local DEM dataset if you want climb profiles
A public URL if you want the shareable ride pages to actually be shareable
whatYouLose: Your riding buddies, who are on the real app and will not install yours
Route push to Garmin and Wahoo head units without a USB cable and a folder full of GPX files
Live rider tracking during the ride, including regrouping and rider-down alerts
A polished mobile app that survives a phone in a jersey pocket at 30 km/h
Discovery of routes other local riders have already built and tested
moatNotes: Every group coordination app has the same shape: the software is simple, the installed base is the product.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the alternative is a group chat where someone posts a Google Maps pin, someone else posts a GPX file that three people cannot open, and two riders show up at the wrong cafe. Velodash's value is that it puts the route, the time, the meeting point, and everyone's live position in one place that the whole bunch already has on their phone. A personal build gives you the route planning, which is the part you were probably fine at anyway, and none of the coordination, which is the part that was actually annoying.
notes: The route planner is a weekend; the bunch ride is not. The moat is that your riding group is already on it and their bike computers talk to it.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted cycling route planner and ride organizer. Single user, runs on my machine, no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud services beyond map tiles.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/rides.db, schema created on first boot
- MapLibre GL JS with raster OpenStreetMap tiles, key-free by default
- Tailwind for styling, no component library

Features, in scope:
1. Route builder: click points on the map to add waypoints, drag to reorder, undo, delete. Snap to roads using the public OSRM demo routing endpoint (base URL in .env so I can swap in my own OSRM later). Show total distance and estimated moving time from an editable average speed.
2. Elevation profile: fetch elevations for the polyline from an endpoint configured in .env (ELEVATION_API_URL). If unset, hide the profile and say so instead of faking numbers.
3. Save routes with name, notes, and a start location label. List page with distance, elevation gain, and a small static map thumbnail rendered client side.
4. GPX import: drag a .gpx file in, parse the track, draw it, save it. GPX export: download a valid GPX 1.1 track for any saved route.
5. Rides: create a ride from a saved route with date, meeting time, meeting point, and a note. Each ride gets a public read-only page at /r/[token] with the map, the profile, the details, and a GPX download button. Tokens are random, unlisted, no auth.
6. Ride log: mark a ride as completed and attach actual distance, time, and a text note. Simple totals per month.

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt:
- Garmin, Wahoo, or Strava integrations
- Live rider location tracking or push notifications
- Invites, RSVPs, chat, or any multi-user accounts
- A native mobile app; make the pages usable on a phone and stop there

Deliver: working app, npm run dev, seed script that inserts two example routes from bundled GPX files, README covering .env keys (TILE_URL, OSRM_URL, ELEVATION_API_URL) and how to expose /r/[token] publicly if I want to. Keep it to one obvious file per concern and do not add auth scaffolding I did not ask for.
